name: trend-only-subsignals-120m-half-band-interior-rebalance
rationale: Cost-side (warning rule; 27th consecutive negative run at 500k), literature-motivated. On 2026-11-16 band-edge + lot round-up was the best variant at every capital (Sharpe +1.38 abs, DD -3.46pp at 50k) but missed the trade-count ratio by 2 trades, and all 11 of its 500k round-ups were one-lot 'top-ups' fired by price drift right after a band-edge trade (post-trade |delta| sits exactly at the threshold, so any drift re-triggers). Holden & Holden show that with proportional costs the optimum rebalances to the no-trade boundary, but with a fixed/minimum-size cost component it rebalances to an interior point. bitFlyer's 0.001 BTC lot floor is such a component. Trading to the midpoint between the band edge and the target (delta - sign*threshold/2) leaves the post-trade allocation threshold/2 inside the band, which should remove drift-triggered top-ups and make more 50k orders clear the lot without round-up.
code_change_summary: Start from experiment/trend-only-subsignals-120m-band-edge-lot-roundup (66a11ec): cherry-pick or merge its commits (trend-only weights TREND 0.25->1.0 / REVERSION 1.0->0.0 with None on weight_sum <= 0.0, band_edge_delta, band_edge_order with lot round-up, and the call-sites in handle_indicator, handle_rebalance and Simulator::run). Update the doc-comment NOTEs to name this hypothesis. Then change band_edge_delta's sizing from the band edge to the interior midpoint: for |delta| > threshold return delta - sign(delta) * threshold / 2 (instead of delta - sign(delta) * threshold); unchanged 0.0 inside the threshold and unchanged delta when threshold == 0. Keep the round-up exactly as on 66a11ec (if the sized order is below min_order_size but the full delta clears it, order exactly min_order_size in delta's direction, never more than the full-delta size). Rename the helper or update its doc comment to say 'half-band interior' and cite Holden & Holden. Rewrite (never delete) the band_edge_delta_* tests for the new expected values and keep the round-up tests. Also run, as an unregistered reference, this branch at 500k with --fee-pct 0 --slippage-pct 0.
constraints: This hypothesis modifies the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. This change MUST be made only on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch -- never as a direct commit to dev/main.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) -- only its body.

MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal's own formula or the aggregation expression; exactly two numeric constants change (TREND 0.25 -> 1.0 and REVERSION 1.0 -> 0.0). Because REVERSION becomes 0.0 the weighted-mean denominator can be zero when only RSI/%B are present (partial warmup): handle that by returning None when weight_sum <= 0.0, and document it.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the compute_btc_target_* unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs -- update their expected values if the new weight legitimately changes them (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, so the reviewer gives it the scrutiny an allocation-formula change deserves.

The band-edge and round-up changes alter only the size of an order that already passes the `delta.abs() >= allocation_threshold` gate; the gate itself and allocation_delta_to_order are unchanged. This touches the live rebalance path in src/trading/engine.rs, so a promoted PR must flag that it changes live order sizing.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the auto-updater.

paper_reference.title: Optimal rebalancing of portfolios with transaction costs
paper_reference.venue_year: Norwegian Computing Center working paper / Stochastics, 2013
paper_reference.key_claim: Transaction costs imply a no-trade region; with proportional costs it is optimal to rebalance to the region's boundary, while with fixed costs the rebalance from outside should be to an interior point of the region.
paper_reference.pros: Directly addresses the observed failure of pure band-edge sizing at 50k: the 0.001 BTC lot minimum behaves like a fixed-size cost, and post-trade drift re-triggering one-lot top-ups was measured on 2026-11-16.
paper_reference.cons: Continuous-time model with a known drift/volatility and a single risky asset, no exchange lot floor or tiered fees; the interior point it derives is not threshold/2 -- that value is a heuristic choice here, not the paper's optimum.
